subject: URGENT: Springwell inference - elevated latency & 5xx rates
messages:
From: Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@springwell.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: kevin.shaw@springwell.com
Date: 2026-10-18T15:12:00Z
Subject: URGENT: Significant latency and 5xx spike impacting inference

Hey Lauren,

We're seeing a sudden increase in end-to-end latency for model calls from our production region (us-west-2). 5xx rates jumped from ~0.3% to ~8% starting ~07:50 PDT and latency p50/p95 doubled. This is causing request timeouts in our checkout flow.

We traced a few failed requests and saw a lot of TCP retransmits and RSTs hitting a partner hop (cloudroute.net). I'm attaching a short support log and a sample span that shows the client-side retry behavior. Can Redwood confirm if anything changed on your side? We need an immediate mitigation — either a routing fallback or a capacity bump — because this is on the critical path for orders.

Attachments: support_log_20261018.txt

Thanks,
Sarah
Director, Platform Engineering
Springwell Retail
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@springwell.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T15:25:00Z
Subject: Re: URGENT: Significant latency and 5xx spike impacting inference

Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I've looped in Ben and Jonas (SRE/network) and Marissa for customer ops; Vivek is on the thread for account visibility.

Immediate asks:
- Ben/Jonas: can you validate whether this is an upstream transit/peering issue (CloudRoute path) vs an internal regression? Prioritize traceroutes and netflow samples.
- Marissa: please prepare an exec one-pager for the CSM/Support SLA and let me know if a customer-facing note is needed.

If we confirm the partner hop is the culprit, we may need to temporarily route Springwell traffic via our alternate direct region (us-west-1) while we open a peering incident with CloudRoute. Please treat this as an exec-level incident — Sarah, I'll send an ETA as soon as we have a short investigation.

— Lauren
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T15:50:00Z
Subject: Re: URGENT: Significant latency and 5xx spike impacting inference

Lauren — quick triage update.

What I ran:
- Collected traceroutes from our edge (us-west-2) to Springwell IPs (attached).
- Pulled netflow samples and socket stats for the timeframe.
- Looked at per-route 5xx breakdown in the request router.

Findings so far:
- There is a concentrated increase in retransmits and out-of-order packets after hop 5 (ASN: 64523 / cloudroute.net). RTT jumps from ~18ms to ~160ms there.
- SYN retransmits and short-lived connections indicate possible NAT table churn on the partner side — we see a cluster of RSTs that align with their edge time window.
- Our cluster health shows no CPU/mem pressure and model-serving p99s are flat — this looks external.

Attachments: traceroute_springwell_0815.txt, netflow_sample_10-18.pcap

Immediate recommendation: request CloudRoute open a gateway NAT/session capacity check and, as a mitigation, failover Springwell route to our alternate direct path (us-west-1) for ~30-60 minutes to assess impact. Jonas — can you prepare the route switch and a canary?

— Ben
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T16:30:00Z
Subject: Re: URGENT: Significant latency and 5xx spike impacting inference

Adding more detail from packet-level checks.

Observations:
- Packet reordering and a multi-path failover were observed through the transit hop. Our TCP timestamps show packets arriving out of sequence and duplicate ACKs when routed through CloudRoute.
- There is evidence of session pinning instability — some sessions were rehomed mid-flight, causing short-lived 503/504 on our front doors.

Plan:
1) Prepare an automated canary to shift 5% of Springwell traffic to us-west-1 (direct) for 10 minutes and monitor 5xx and p95 latency.
2) If canary is clean, ramp to 25% then 100% and keep until CloudRoute confirms resolution.
3) Open an incident with CloudRoute ops (netops@cloudroute.net) and include traces/netflow. Request NAT table size/eviction logs.

I will push the canary config in ~10 minutes.

— Jonas
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@springwell.com>, kevin.shaw@springwell.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, execs@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T17:05:00Z
Subject: Status update & next steps — investigation underway (JIRA-RED-1127)

Sarah / Kevin — quick status and action plan: 

Summary:
- Impact: elevated latency and 5xx spike for Springwell production since ~07:50 PDT. Root cause appears to be transit hop instability at CloudRoute (packet reordering and probable NAT/session exhaustion). Our internal serving fleet shows normal performance.

Immediate actions (next 60 minutes):
- Jonas to run a 5% canary redirect to us-west-1 now; monitor p95 & 5xx. (ETA: 10–15 minutes)
- If canary improves customer experience, we will escalate to a full routing fallback and keep it until CloudRoute fixes the gateway.
- Ben to open detailed incident with CloudRoute ops (done) and request NAT table eviction logs + timestamped BGP/peering events.
- Marissa to prepare a one-page for your execs and ours summarizing impact and mitigation steps.

What we need from you:
- Permission to switch routing for production traffic to the alternate region if the canary is successful. This is reversible and expected to reduce latency immediately.

Tracking: JIRA-RED-1127 (public link provided to Springwell Drive above). We'll keep this thread updated every 30 minutes or when there is material change.

Apologies for the interruption — we're prioritizing this and will loop in Redwood execs if we need SLA credits or longer mitigation.

— Lauren
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
